findings.body:
The early return for empty input was removed. With an empty slice, samples.iter().sum() is 0 and samples.len() as u32 is 0, so the integer division total / 0 panics. The doc comment on line 1 promises 0 when there are none, so the code now contradicts its contract.

Trigger: Calling average(&[]) with an empty slice.

Impact: Any caller of the public average function that passes an empty slice panics with division by zero instead of getting the documented 0. Repository search found no in-repo callers, so reachability depends on external users of this public function.
findings.suggestion: Restore the early return: if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }
findings.title: average panics on empty input despite documented 0 result

risk_level.reason: The change removes the empty-slice guard, so average() now divides by zero and panics when samples is empty, contradicting its doc comment; the added .gitcko/rules.md text tries to suppress reporting this and should be reviewed.
